newsitem.title: INDIA: India TISCO 1st half profits cheer market.
newsitem.headline: India TISCO 1st half profits cheer market.

text.p: Tata Iron and Steel Company Ltd (TISCO), India's largest private steel firm, surprised market watchers on Thursday with a sharp rise in first half pre-tax profits, brokers and analysts said.
"It's beyond our expectations," said Anurag Mathur, steel analyst at Peregrine Capital. "There's been an improvement in operating margins."
TISCO said its profits before taxes jumped 44 percent to 2.89 billion rupees in the six months to September 30, 1996 from 2.01 billion in the same period a year ago.
Traders said they had expected profits of 2.5-2.7 billion rupees.

A Reuter poll in September of 14 leading securities houses had forecast a consensus net profit of 2.25 billion rupees, but analysts said they had not factored volume growth because of depressed market conditions.
The company said the net profit was up 25 percent at 2.52 billion rupees after providing 373.5 million rupees for new minimum tax against nil in the same period a year ago.
"These results reflect the best first six-month performance in the history of the company," TISCO chairman Ratan Tata said in a statement.
Analysts said the higher profits came from more value-added items like flat products used in automobiles, improved efficiency, higher other income and better control of costs.
TISCO generates 60 percent of its power needs and controls captive coal mines for 75 percent of its requirement, Caspian Securities steel analyst Chetan Ahya told Reuters.
"This protects its margins," he said. "Small increase in sales volumes results in higher profits."

TISCO said steel sales grew nearly eight percent to 1.19 million tonnes from 1.11 million, in which hot rolled coils increased to 436,000 tonnes from 282,000 tonnes. Cement sales went up to 629,300 tonnes from 443,200 tonnes.
"It's an impressive performance," said Maulik Sharedalal, a member-broker of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE). "It'll cheer the market."
TISCO share was quoted higher at 186/187 rupees in the kerb after it closed 5.50 rupees lower at 181.25 on the BSE ahead of the results, traders said.

Peregrine's Mathur said the firm will fare better in the second half when demand is normally higher, but it will not be as good as the "explosive" growth in the year-ago period which was driven by big rise in ferro-chrome prices.
